AfterDamageGiven.maps_to: on_block_broken (hand_drill.py:21-29) -- the port re-hooks C#'s AfterDamageGiven-with-a-WasBlockBroken-guard onto the sim's dedicated on_block_broken event, dispatched from inside DamageCmd.deal's block absorption (cmds.py:81)
AfterDamageGiven.rationale: HandDrill.cs:22-29 fires on AfterDamageGiven and self-filters to `result.WasBlockBroken`; the sim listens on on_block_broken instead, whose firing condition cmds.py:76-81 implements as `target.block == 0` after absorbing inside `if target.block > 0 and UNBLOCKABLE not in props` -- i.e. exactly C#'s `Block <= 0 && blockedDamage > 0` (CreatureCmd.cs:273, and damage_pipeline spec step 14 verdicts that equivalence faithful). The two C# hooks are two lines apart in the same per-result loop (AfterBlockBroken at CreatureCmd.cs:376-379, AfterDamageGiven at :388-391), so the trigger SET is identical; what differs is that the sim's event fires during absorption, before HP loss, which audit/records/seam/damage_pipeline.json guard N5 verdicts deliberate-divergence and which NAMES HAND DRILL as one of its two ported listeners. One verdict per mechanism, binding rule 3: matched, not re-derived. EXECUTED (py audit/tools/relic_probes_b07.py drill-vuln): an exact break and an overkill break each leave the enemy with Vulnerable 2; a partial hit and a no-block hit leave it with none; a killing blow that also breaks block still applies Vulnerable (C# agrees -- AfterDamageGiven is not killing-blow-guarded, damage_pipeline spec step 17.4); and an ENEMY breaking the PLAYER's block applies nothing. Rule 7: CreatureCmd.cs, sts2_rl/cmds.py and the damage_pipeline record are not hashed by this record.

guards.what: G1 (DORMANT): C# orders AfterBlockBroken listeners BEFORE AfterDamageGiven listeners for the same damage result; the sim puts Hand Drill on the same event as the AfterBlockBroken listener and lets registration order decide
guards.issue: MECHANISM: CreatureCmd.cs:376-391 runs `Hook.AfterBlockBroken` and then `Hook.AfterDamageGiven` as separate statements in the per-result loop, so every AfterBlockBroken implementer is guaranteed to run before Hand Drill. In the sim both are on_block_broken (hooks.py:490-498), a single listener walk, and relics are registered at CombatState construction while powers register when applied -- so Hand Drill runs FIRST. DORMANT, with the population enumerated by execution: `grep -rn 'AfterBlockBroken' src/Core/Models/` returns exactly ONE override in the whole game, BurrowedPower.cs:24, whose effect is to stun its own owner and drop its block (mirrored at powers.py:2293-2300); it reads no power on the target and applies none, so neither order changes an outcome. Concrete triggers: a second AfterBlockBroken implementer whose effect the Vulnerable would interact with, or an ENEMY carrying Artifact (which would consume the first debuff applied and so make the order decide WHICH power is negated) -- note PROMPT.md bug class 6's warning that a player holding Artifact does not exist in the game, but the enemy side is a separate question this batch did not settle. Rule 7: CreatureCmd.cs, BurrowedPower.cs, sts2_rl/hooks.py, sts2_rl/powers.py and sts2_rl/combat.py are not hashed by this record.

guards.what: G2 (DORMANT): the C# guard is `dealer == base.Owner.Creature || dealer?.PetOwner == base.Owner` -- the port drops the PET arm entirely (hand_drill.py:22 is `dealer is not self.player`)
guards.issue: MECHANISM: HandDrill.cs:24 credits the owner's PET's damage to the owner, so an Osty (or any relic-granted pet) that breaks an enemy's block also triggers Hand Drill. The sim has no pet concept at all -- executed: `grep -rn 'pet_owner\|PetOwner' sts2_rl/ --include=*.py` returns ZERO hits -- so the arm has nothing to test. DORMANT, and the concrete unported thing is named: Osty is the Necrobinder's pet and pet-granting relics are declared but not implemented (relics/base.py:91-92 carries an `adds_pet` FLAG for Pael's Legion with no creature behind it, and damage_pipeline spec step 10 waives the Osty damage-redirection hook for the same reason). Porting a pet makes it live. Filed as a gap rather than waived because 'the sim has no pets' is today's content and not the divergence's shape (binding rule 1); note it is NOT an other-character waiver, since Pael's Legion is an Ironclad-reachable relic. Rule 7: relics/base.py, relics/paels_legion.py and the damage_pipeline record are not hashed by this record.

guards.what: N1: `!target.IsPlayer` (HandDrill.cs:24) vs `target is self.player` (hand_drill.py:22) -- identity, not the IsPlayer predicate
guards.rationale: The sim's combat holds exactly one player creature (CombatState keeps `player` plus an enemy list), so `is self.player` and `not target.IsPlayer` select the same set today. Executed (probe drill-vuln): an enemy breaking the player's block applies nothing. Recorded rather than skipped because a ported player-side non-player creature would separate the two -- C# would still refuse to Vulnerable it (it is not IsPlayer, so the clause PASSES and the relic WOULD fire on a friendly minion), which means the sim is currently the stricter of the two and the difference is C#'s, not the port's. Worth naming so a future minion port re-reads the clause instead of assuming the port is right.

guards.what: N2: PowerVar<VulnerablePower>(2m) (HandDrill.cs:18) read as `base.DynamicVars.Vulnerable.BaseValue` at the call site (line 27) vs the sim's VULNERABLE = 2 (hand_drill.py:19)
guards.rationale: No AscensionHelper.GetValueIfAscension anywhere in the file, so 2 is the pinned non-ascension value. Note the read is the PROPERTY form (`DynamicVars.Vulnerable`) where relic/gorget in this batch uses the keyed form for the same PowerVar<T> construction -- the same source inconsistency bronze_scales guard N2 records, harmless because both resolve to the one registered var.

guards.what: N3: applier = `base.Owner.Creature` and cardSource = null (HandDrill.cs:27); the sim passes applier=self.player and no card (hand_drill.py:26-29)
guards.rationale: Matched, and load-bearing in both directions. applier=player is what lets relic/unsettling_lamp's doubling see this Vulnerable at all (its modify_power_amount requires `applier is self.player`), so a port that omitted the applier would silently halve a Lamp+Drill deck's Vulnerable; and cardSource=null is what keeps it OUT of the Lamp's cardSource latch, since the Lamp needs a triggering card. Checked deliberately against belt_buckle guard N3 (both null) and gorget guard N3 (applier only) in the same batch. Rule 7: relics/unsettling_lamp.py is not hashed by this record.

guards.what: N4: the port passes `self.combat.hooks` where its siblings pass `self.hooks` (hand_drill.py:27)
guards.rationale: Relic.hooks is defined as `self.combat.hooks` (relics/base.py:287-288), so the two spellings are the same object. Recorded only because the inconsistency looks like it might indicate a different dispatcher and does not. Rule 7: relics/base.py is not hashed by this record.

guards.what: N5: Flash(), the Vulnerable hover tip and the unused `props` / `result` / `choiceContext` parameters (HandDrill.cs:20, 22, 26)
guards.rationale: RelicModel.Flash() / FlashSfx / base.Status / ShowCounter / DisplayAmount / InvokeDisplayAmountChanged / CanonicalVars / ExtraHoverTips / Cmd.Wait / CardCmd.PreviewCardPileAdd are presentation only -- the relic bar's glow, counter, sfx and hover text, and animation timing. The sim has no relic UI. Waived under the shared contract's presentation/animation exclusion, not under an unreachability claim. The parameters the relic does not read are covered by the same waiver as the multiplayer plumbing (hook_dispatch guard N1); `result` IS read, for WasBlockBroken, and that read is the hook entry's subject.
